LESSON: MELODY

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.4: Melody

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Melody. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can a melody be made interesting?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. describe the use of variation in composing a melody
2. compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 4 time
3. perform melodies in F major and 4 4 time
4. value the use of melody in Creative Arts and Sports

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MELODY
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Melody helps you succeed in CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MELODY
Study Melody like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Describe the use of variation in composing a melody

What this means
In this part you learn to describe the use of variation in composing a melody. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: describe the use of variation in composing a melody.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can describe the use of variation in composing a melody. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 4 time

What this means
In this part you learn to compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 4 time. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 4 time.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Melody in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 4 time. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Perform melodies in F major and 4 4 time

What this means
In this part you learn to perform melodies in F major and 4 4 time. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: perform melodies in F major and 4 4 time.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can perform melodies in F major and 4 4 time. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Value the use of melody in Creative Arts and Sports

What this means
In this part you learn to value the use of melody in Creative Arts and Sports. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: value the use of melody in Creative Arts and Sports.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can value the use of melody in Creative Arts and Sports. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Melody is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: describe the use of variation in composing a melody)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Melody in your own words. (skill: compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 4 time)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: perform melodies in F major and 4 4 time)

Example 4: Show how “Melody” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: value the use of melody in Creative Arts and Sports)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Melody to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: describe the use of variation in composing a melody.
3. Practise this skill: compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 4 time.
4. Practise this skill: perform melodies in F major and 4 4 time.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Melody from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Melody: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Melody?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can a melody be made interesting?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Melody means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: describe the use of variation in composing a melody.
5. Be able to: compose a four-bar melody in F Major and 4 4 time.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
